items.title: Complete symmetrized constant-coefficient evolution
items.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $m\ge1$, let $U:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^m$, and let $A_1,A_2,A_3,B,M\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$ be constant matrices. Assume $M=M^{\mathsf T}$ is positive definite, each $MA_j$ is symmetric, and $S:=(MB+B^{\mathsf T}M)/2$ is positive semidefinite. Consider

$$\partial_tU+\sum_{j=1}^3A_j\partial_{x_j}U+BU=0.$$

Use [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]: for $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and multi-indices $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb N^3$, the scalar seminorm is $p_{\alpha\beta}(f):=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^3}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|$, and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$ consists of functions for which all these seminorms are finite. Here $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^m)$ means maps $U=(U_1,\ldots,U_m)$ with real-valued components such that each component, viewed as complex-valued with zero imaginary part, belongs to $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$; its vector seminorms are $p_{\alpha\beta}^{(m)}(U):=\max_{1\leq\ell\leq m}p_{\alpha\beta}(U_\ell)$. For $U_0\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^m)$ there is a unique global smooth solution, Schwartz in $x$ at each time and continuous in every $p_{\alpha\beta}^{(m)}$ on compact time intervals. With the negative-sign, $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform, put $\widehat U(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}U(x)\,dx$ and define, for $s\ge0$,

$$\|U\|_{H^s_M}^2:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}(1+|\xi|^2)^s\widehat U(\xi)^*M\widehat U(\xi)\,d\xi.$$

For $t\ge0$, $\|U(t)\|_{H^s_M}\le\|U_0\|_{H^s_M}$ for every $s\ge0$; hence the solution depends continuously on the data in each such norm. The same conclusions hold for smooth periodic data on the flat torus $\mathbb T_L^3:=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$, $L>0$, with Fourier coefficients $\widehat U_k=L^{-3}\int_{[0,L]^3}U(x)e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x/L}\,dx$ and

$$\|U\|_{H^s_M(\mathbb T_L^3)}^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k/L|^2)^s\widehat U_k^*M\widehat U_k.$$

For periodic data, $\|U(t)\|_\infty\le C_{s,L,M}\|U_0\|_{H^s_M(\mathbb T_L^3)}$ for each integer $s>3/2$.

For a unit vector $\nu\in\mathbb R^3$, write $A(\nu)=\sum_j\nu_jA_j$ and $\widetilde A(\nu)=M^{1/2}A(\nu)M^{-1/2}$. The finite speed

$$v_*:=\sup_{|\nu|=1}\max\{|\lambda|:\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(\widetilde A(\nu))\}$$

is finite. If $v_*>0$, $R>v_*t$, and $U_0$ vanishes on $B_R(x_0)$, then $U(t)$ vanishes on $B_{R-v_*t}(x_0)$ for $0\le t<R/v_*$. The same assertion holds on $\mathbb T_L^3$ using its geodesic distance. If $v_*=0$, every $A_j=0$ and the system is a pointwise linear ODE, so spatial support does not move. These are conclusions for the displayed linear systems; no variable-coefficient or nonlinear existence claim is included.

items.title: Perfect sound characteristic and actual stable causal linear branch
items.statement:
Fix $c>0$ and take $M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,\mathbf x)$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and future causal cone $\{V\in\mathbb R^4:V^0\geq0,\ \eta_{ab}V^aV^b\leq0\}$. For $V=(V^0,\mathbf V)\in\mathbb R^4$ with $V^0>0$, define its coordinate velocity by $\mathbf v(V):=c\mathbf V/V^0$. Since $\eta(V,V)=(V^0)^2(|\mathbf v(V)|^2/c^2-1)$, membership in this cone is equivalent to $|\mathbf v(V)|\leq c$, with equality on its nonzero null boundary. The zero vector belongs to the cone but has no coordinate velocity under this definition. The constant rest observer is $\bar u=(1,0,0,0)$.

Let $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be open, let $e\in C^2(X;\mathbb R)$, and fix $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})\in X$. Define $n_0:=1/v_0$, $\epsilon_0:=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $p_0:=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $T_0:=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, and $h_0:=\epsilon_0+p_0$. Assume $n_0,T_0,h_0,e_{vv}>0$, with $e_{vv}$ evaluated at fixed $\sigma_p$. A first variation is defined by a family of state maps $(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda}):M\to X$ and fields $u_\lambda:M\to\mathbb R^4$, jointly smooth in dimensionless $\lambda$ near $0$ and in $x$, with the displayed reference state and $\bar u$ as their constant $\lambda=0$ values and with $\eta(u_\lambda,u_\lambda)=-1$, $u_\lambda^0>0$. For any such field $f_\lambda$, write $\delta f:=\left.\partial_\lambda f_\lambda\right|_{\lambda=0}$; put $r:=\delta\epsilon$, $w:=(\delta u^1,\delta u^2,\delta u^3)$, and impose the adiabatic first-variation condition $\delta\sigma_p=0$. The linearized equations mean the first variations at $\lambda=0$ of the no-force balances $\partial_aT_\lambda^{ab}=0$ and $\partial_aJ_\lambda^a=0$, with $n_\lambda=1/v_\lambda$, $\epsilon_\lambda=n_\lambda e(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $p_\lambda=-e_v(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $\Delta_\lambda^{ab}=\eta^{ab}+u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b$, $T_\lambda^{ab}=\epsilon_\lambda u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b+p_\lambda\Delta_\lambda^{ab}$, and $J_\lambda^a=n_\lambda u_\lambda^a$; no member with $\lambda\ne0$ is required to solve the nonlinear balances. Differentiating $\eta(u_\lambda,u_\lambda)=-1$ gives $\delta u^0=0$.

The local Gibbs identity of [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]] gives

$$a_s:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\epsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})}{n_0h_0},$$

and assume additionally $a_s\le1$. In the adopted units, $c$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $r$ and $h_0$ have units Pa, and $w$ and $a_s$ are dimensionless. Since $x^0=ct$ and $\bar u=\partial_{x^0}$, the first variations of the no-force perfect-fluid projection equations of [[lem-tgr-perfect-fluid-projection]] are

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c a_s}{h_0}\nabla r=0.$$

For initial data $U_0=(r_0,w_0)$ whose real components belong componentwise to $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$ as defined by [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]], or for smooth periodic data on $\mathbb T_L^3$ with $L>0$, these equations have the unique global smooth solution supplied by [[lem-tgr-constant-linear-energy-causality]]. The positive quadratic energy density $\mathcal E=\tfrac12[(a_s/h_0)r^2+h_0|w|^2]$ has flux $c a_s r w$, and the solution is contractive in the corresponding weighted $L^2$ and Sobolev norms. Its characteristic speeds are $0$ and $\pm c\sqrt{a_s}$; for positive $a_s$, this propagation cone lies inside the Minkowski reference cone exactly when $a_s\le1$. These are statements about this frozen linear system only; they do not assert a nonlinear or curved-spacetime evolution theorem.

For the formal coefficient comparison in [A3], if the same linear equations are assigned $a_s>1$, their plane-wave speed is $c\sqrt{a_s}>c$. If they are assigned $a_s<0$, smooth periodic modes grow as $e^{c\sqrt{-a_s}|k|t}$ at arbitrarily large wave numbers. The case $a_s=0$ is degenerate: the displayed positive energy matrix is no longer positive definite, so the stability proof above does not apply.

items.title: Corrected bulk relaxation and exact extended entropy
items.statement:
Use the smooth $(-,+,+,+)$ Lorentzian data, local state, and conventions of [[lem-tgr-perfect-fluid-projection]] and [[lem-tgr-dissipative-entropy-identity]], with $n>0$, $T>0$, $c>0$, $x^0=ct$, and smooth future unit $u$. On the nonempty open spacetime domain $O$ of those suppliers, let $\zeta,\tau\in C^1(O;(0,\infty))$ be scalar coefficient fields, set $\beta:=\tau/\zeta\in C^1(O;(0,\infty))$, and let $\Pi:O\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. In the bulk-only branch take

$$T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a,\qquad \nabla_aT^{ab}=0,\qquad \nabla_aJ^a=0,$$

where $\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, $\theta=\nabla_au^a$, and $a^b_{\rm acc}=Du^b$. Adopt the corrected relaxation law

$$\beta D\Pi+\frac{\Pi}{\zeta c}=-\theta-\frac{T\Pi}{2}\nabla_a\!\left(\frac{\beta u^a}{T}\right)$$

and the extended entropy current $S^a=[s-\beta\Pi^2/(2T)]u^a$. Then the stress and particle equations imply

$$D\epsilon+(h+\Pi)\theta=0,\qquad (h+\Pi)a^b_{\rm acc}+\Delta^{ba}\nabla_a(p+\Pi)=0,\qquad Dn+n\theta=0,$$

and every actual smooth solution of the stated corrected law satisfies

$$\nabla_aS^a=\frac{\Pi^2}{\zeta cT}\ge0.$$

Here $\beta$ has units $\mathrm{Pa^{-1}}$, $\Pi,\epsilon,p,h$ have units Pa, $D,\theta,a_{\rm acc}$ have inverse-length components, and the correction $\beta\Pi^2/(2T)$ has the units of entropy density. The law is an explicit model assumption; dropping its derivative term does not yield the stated sign identity in general.

There is an exact homogeneous solution on the explicitly specified Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and future direction $\partial_{x^0}$; its Levi-Civita derivative is ordinary coordinate differentiation. Fix a state point $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$ in the supplied local state domain with $v_0>0$ and $T_0=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})>0$, and take the constant state map $(v,\sigma_p)(x)=(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, so $n_0=1/v_0$, $\epsilon_0=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, and $p_0=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$ are constant. For constant positive coefficients $\zeta_0,\tau_0$, let $u=\partial_{x^0}=(1,0,0,0)$, $T=T_0$, and define the smooth scalar field $\Pi(x)=\Pi_0e^{-t/\tau_0}$ on all of $M$, where $t=x^0/c$. The stress and particle balances and the corrected law hold, with strict entropy production wherever $\Pi(x)\ne0$. This mathematical witness is not a general nonlinear existence theorem or a claim of physical applicability in any separately selected near-equilibrium regime.

items.title: Bulk linear relaxation energy, stability and causal speed
items.statement:
Use $\mathcal M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,\mathbf x)$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, future direction $\partial_{x^0}$, and reference causal cone $\{V\in\mathbb R^4:V^0\geq0,\ \eta_{ab}V^aV^b\leq0\}$. For $V=(V^0,\mathbf V)$ with $V^0>0$, define $\mathbf v(V):=c\mathbf V/V^0$; then $\eta(V,V)=(V^0)^2(|\mathbf v(V)|^2/c^2-1)$, so cone membership is equivalent to $|\mathbf v(V)|\leq c$, with equality on its nonzero null boundary. The zero vector belongs to the cone but has no coordinate velocity under this definition. Let $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be open, $e\in C^2(X;\mathbb R)$, and $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})\in X$. Define $n_0:=1/v_0$, $\epsilon_0:=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $p_0:=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $T_0:=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, and $h_0:=\epsilon_0+p_0$. The background fields are this constant state, $u_0=\partial_{x^0}=(1,0,0,0)$, and $\Pi_0=0$. Assume $n_0,T_0,h_0,e_{vv},c>0$, with $e_{vv}$ evaluated at fixed $\sigma_p$.

A first variation is defined by a family $(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda},u_\lambda,\Pi_\lambda)$ jointly smooth in dimensionless $\lambda$ near $0$ and in $x$, through the displayed background, with $u_\lambda$ future unit, meaning $\eta(u_\lambda,u_\lambda)=-1$ and $u_\lambda^0>0$. For any such field $f_\lambda$, set $\delta f:=\left.\partial_\lambda f_\lambda\right|_{\lambda=0}$. At each $\lambda$, set $n_\lambda=1/v_\lambda$, $\epsilon_\lambda=n_\lambda e(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $p_\lambda=-e_v(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $T_\lambda=e_{\sigma_p}(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $\Delta_\lambda^{ab}=\eta^{ab}+u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b$, $D_\lambda=u_\lambda^a\partial_a$, and $\theta_\lambda=\partial_a u_\lambda^a$. The bulk stress and current are $T_\lambda^{ab}=\epsilon_\lambda u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b+(p_\lambda+\Pi_\lambda)\Delta_\lambda^{ab}$ and $J_\lambda^a=n_\lambda u_\lambda^a$, and the corrected law of [[lem-tgr-bulk-relaxation-entropy]] is $\beta D_\lambda\Pi_\lambda+\Pi_\lambda/(\zeta c)=-\theta_\lambda-(T_\lambda\Pi_\lambda/2)\partial_a(\beta u_\lambda^a/T_\lambda)$, where $\beta=\tau/\zeta$. The linearized equations mean the first variations at $\lambda=0$ of $\partial_aT_\lambda^{ab}=0$, $\partial_aJ_\lambda^a=0$, and this corrected law, set equal to zero; no member with $\lambda\ne0$ is required to solve the nonlinear system. Impose $\delta\sigma_p=0$, put $r:=\delta\epsilon$, $w:=(\delta u^1,\delta u^2,\delta u^3)$, and denote $\delta\Pi$ by $\Pi$ in the linearized system below. Take constant coefficients $\zeta,\tau>0$.

$$a_s:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\epsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}}{n_0h_0}>0$$

as supplied by [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]]. The resulting linearized system is

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c}{h_0}\nabla(a_s r+\Pi)=0,\qquad \tau\Pi_t+\Pi=-\zeta c\operatorname{div}w.$$

Its positive quadratic energy density

$$\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}=\frac12\left[\frac{a_s}{h_0}r^2+h_0|w|^2+\frac{\tau}{\zeta}\Pi^2\right]$$

satisfies $\partial_t\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}+\operatorname{div}[c(a_s r+\Pi)w]=-\Pi^2/\zeta$. The normal characteristic speeds are $0$ and $\pm v_{\rm bulk}$, where

$$v_{\rm bulk}=c\sqrt{a_s+\frac{\zeta}{\tau h_0}}.$$

By [[lem-tgr-constant-linear-energy-causality]], initial data $U_0\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^5)$ with the componentwise real convention of [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]], or smooth periodic data on $\mathbb T_L^3$ with $L>0$, have unique global smooth solutions, contractive in the corresponding energy and Sobolev norms, with finite propagation at $v_{\rm bulk}$. The branch is inside the Minkowski reference cone exactly when $a_s+\zeta/(\tau h_0)\le1$. Constant density and transverse velocity modes can persist, so contraction does not mean every mode decays. No nonlinear or variable-coefficient existence theorem is claimed.

items.title: Positive relaxation parameters can give superluminal characteristic speed
items.statement:
Choose $n_0,T_0,h_0,\tau,c>0$ and $\sigma_{p0}\in\mathbb R$, put $v_0=1/n_0$, and on an open neighborhood $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ of $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$ define the $C^2$ local energy per marker

$$e(v,\sigma_p)=\frac{h_0}{n_0}+T_0(\sigma_p-\sigma_{p0})+\frac{n_0h_0}{6}(v-v_0)^2.$$

Choose $X$ small enough that $v>0$ and the local enthalpy density $h:=\epsilon+p$, with $n=1/v$, $\epsilon=ne$, and $p=-e_v$, remains positive. At the reference state, $T=e_{\sigma_p}=T_0>0$, $p_0=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})=0$, $\epsilon_0=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})=h_0$, and $e_{vv}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})=n_0h_0/3$. The local Gibbs response in [[lem-tgr-bulk-linear-causality]] therefore realizes $a_s=e_{vv}/(n_0h_0)=1/3$. Now set $\zeta=\tau h_0$. All positivity hypotheses of that bulk linear branch hold, but its exact normal characteristic speed is $v_{\rm bulk}=c\sqrt{1/3+1}=2c/\sqrt3>c$. With SI units, $h_0$ is in Pa and $\tau$ in s, so $\zeta$ is in Pa s. This is a parameterized mathematical model example, not a measurement or an estimate for a material.
